item.title: Hillary Clinton Faces Closed-Door Deposition in Oversight Committee’s Epstein Probe
item.description: Former Secretary of State and former First Lady, Hillary Clinton, faced questions behind closed doors in Chappaqua, New York on Thursday. The deposition in the Clintons’ hometown is part of the Republican-led House Oversight Committee’s probe into convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Judge Allows Trump’s White House Ballroom Construction to Move Forward
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - A US district judge rejects a request to block the President’s $400,000 ballroom project.

item.title: White House Sends Democrats Counteroffer for DHS Funding
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - Congressional members left DC this weekend without finalizing a deal to end the Department of Homeland Security shutdown.

item.title: Bill Clinton Sits for Closed-Door Deposition in House Panel’s Epstein Investigation
item.description: Former President Bill Clinton fielded questions Friday in front of the House Oversight Committee during an hours-long closed-door deposition in Chappaqua, New York. The highly anticipated deposition is part of the House Oversight Committee’s ongoing investigation into the late, convicted sex offender, Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Iranian-Americans Celebrate Death of Supreme Leader, Discuss Steps Toward Regime Change
item.description: The United States and Israel have launched a major military offensive against Iran, marking a dramatic escalation in Middle East tensions. President Donald Trump confirmed Saturday afternoon that Iran’s supreme leader, Ali Khamenei, has been killed in the targeted strikes by the U.S. and Israel.

item.title: US Central Command: Minimal Damage to US Installations in Strikes Against Iran, 3 Service Members Killed
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - President Donald Trump said Iran’s Supreme Leader has been killed. This follows an intensive strike between US and Israeli forces early Saturday morning. Experts said the killing could have a huge political shift in Iran and the Middle East.

item.title: Three US Service Members Killed, US Central Command Update
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - US Central Command released an update following the US-Israeli strike on Iran. They said as of 9:30 am ET, March 1, three US service members have been killed in action and five are seriously wounded as part of Operation Epic Fury.

item.title: Additional US Forces Head to Middle East, No Set Timeline Ending Military Operations in Iran
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - US Central Command now confirms in total four US service members have died following Operation Epic Fury, the joint military operation with Israel, which struck Iran. The Pentagon said more casualties could happen and didn’t specify how long US operations in Iran could last.

item.title: U.S. Offensive in Iran Sparks Escalation Abroad, War Powers Debate on Capitol Hill
item.description: Following the sweeping military offensive against Iran over the weekend, which resulted in the death of Iran’s supreme leader and dozens of top commanders, President Donald Trump said the operations will continue.
